subject: Pilot delivery-profile: clarify time-to-first-token and sustained-rate expectations
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@lumenhealth.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumen Health Technical <infra@lumenhealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot SLA questions: streaming vs sync delivery profiles

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is keen to start the 8-week pilot. Before we kick off procurement we need a short, clear statement of what Redwood will commit to for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints. Our infra team is specifically asking for:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations (p95, p99) for streaming endpoints at our expected request sizes (~30 tokens prompt + up to 250 response tokens).
- Sustained token/sec expectations per session and burst behaviour (how long can a customer sustain a high token/sec window before throttling?)
- Fallback behaviour: if streaming availability drops, do you provide a non-streaming (batch) fallback and what are latency tradeoffs?

We don't need final contract language right now, just a one-page operational summary so our procurement/security folks can sign off on the pilot.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ramos
Head of Product Integrations, Lumen Health

Attachment: initial_pilot_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@lumenhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions: streaming vs sync delivery profiles

Hi Sofia — rapid response from our side. High-level answers first, then I'll attach a one-page operational summary (PDF) and the pilot route config we suggest.

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints- Target: p95 TTFT <= 250 ms for typical request size (prompt ~30 input tokens) when routed to the primary capacity pool in the us-west region.- Guardrail: p99 TTFT <= 450 ms.- Notes: TTFT is measured from request accept to first token output for streaming sessions. Very long prompts and models with large context windows can increase kernel compilation/LLM latency and may push p99 higher.

2) Sustained token/sec expectations- Baseline sustained rate: 30 tokens/sec per active stream session (this is what we can guarantee under committed capacity).- Burst: short bursts up to 80 tokens/sec per session for up to 45 seconds (subject to pool headroom).- Throttling: sustained >30 tokens/sec beyond 45s will be rate-limited (we will return 429-based pacing headers and a recommended client retry-backoff).

3) Fallback behaviour- If the streaming runtime is congested or an upstream failure occurs, we offer an automatic fallback to non-streaming (synchronous) endpoints. Typical impact: median end-to-end latency increases (non-streamed generation completes at the same cost but will deliver payload once finished).

What I'm attaching: a short SLA sketch (Lumen_Pilot_SLA_Draft.pdf) with the above numbers and a sample pilot-routes YAML that pins the pilot to our dedicated pool. If that looks ok, Marissa / Ben can help convert into contract wording and SLO clauses.

Next steps: would you like the SLA expressed as p95/p99 or p50/p95? Our legal typically wants p95/p99 for availability metrics.

Best,
Mateo
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Lumen_Pilot_SLA_Draft.pdf (pdf), pilot-routes-configuration.yaml (yaml)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions: streaming vs sync delivery profiles

On Tue, Jan 19, 2027 at 11:04 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints
> - Target: p95 TTFT <= 250 ms ...
> 2) Sustained token/sec expectations
> - Baseline sustained rate: 30 tokens/sec per active stream session...

Quick internal notes and asks before we finalize language for procurement:

- Instrumentation: we need to ensure the pilot includes token-level traces and per-request SLI logging so Lumen can see p95/p99 broken down by model variant + prompt length. Add this to the pilot config.
- Rollout policy: recommend we include an explicit canary (10% traffic) for the first 72 hours and measure TTFT and sustained rates. If p95 breaches the threshold for 2 consecutive 1-hour windows, auto-fallback to sync for the canary group.
- Quantization/Model variant: call out that the guarantees assume the model configuration we tested (quantized 4-bit variant). If they swap to larger or non-quantized variants we need to re-evaluate.

Ben: can you draft a short fallback paragraph we can put directly into the one-pager (legal likes concise operational statements)?

--
Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions: streaming vs sync delivery profiles

Marissa / Mateo,

Draft fallback wording below — feel free to copy into the PDF. Short + prescriptive:

Redwood provides a streaming-first delivery profile for this pilot. If streaming delivery experiences sustained degradation (defined as p95 TTFT > 400 ms OR sustained-rate violations in two consecutive 1-hour windows for >10% of active sessions), Redwood will automatically route affected requests to a synchronous (non-streaming) delivery profile. Under fallback, customers should expect completion latency to increase (completion-based response delivered at finish) and for streaming-specific latency SLIs to no longer apply for those routed requests. Redwood will log all fallback events and provide a report within 24 hours.

Operationally: we will expose pacing headers and a /metrics endpoint. We'll also provide a daily digest of TTFT and sustained-rate percentiles for the pilot.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@lumenhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions: streaming vs sync delivery profiles

Hi Sofia — attaching the one-page summary and pilot config we discussed. Below is the condensed operational summary we propose for procurement:

- TTFT (streaming): p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 450 ms (measured per request; baseline testing with 30-token prompts).
- Sustained rate: guaranteed 30 tokens/sec per active streaming session; burst to 80 tokens/sec for up to 45 seconds. Sustained >30 tokens/sec beyond 45s may be rate-limited with pacing headers and 429 backoff.
- Fallback: automatic routing to synchronous delivery if streaming falls below thresholds (see Ben's fallback wording for exact triggers). Redwood will provide token-level SLI logs, a /metrics endpoint, and a daily digest.

If that matches Lumen's needs we'll prepare an SLO appendix with the exact p95/p99 measurement windows and a 72-hour canary plan. Please confirm whether you want us to express availability as p95/p99 or p50/p95 for the pilot deliverable.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started next week.

Best,
Mateo
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Lumen_Pilot_SLA_Draft.pdf, pilot-routes-configuration.yaml
